In [[mathematical logic]], an '''elementary definition''' is a definition that can be made using only [[finitary]] [[first-order logic]], and in particular without reference to [[set theory]] or using extensions such as [[plural quantification]]. Elementary definitions are of particular interest because they [[Gödel's_completeness_theorem|admit a complete proof apparatus]] while still being expressive enough to support most everyday mathematics (via the addition of elementarily-expressible axioms such as [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory]] (ZFC)).

Saying that a definition is elementary is a weaker condition than saying it is algebraic.
